review.brief_reason: The only change is log(sqrt(x3)) -> log(x3)/2. Under gplearn protected semantics (log(a)=log(|a|) when |a|>0.001 else 0), the original evaluates to 0.5*log|x3| whenever sqrt(|x3|)>0.001, i.e. |x3|>1e-6, while the proposed yields 0.5*log|x3| only when |x3|>0.001 and 0 otherwise. They therefore disagree on 1e-6<|x3|<=0.001, which lies inside the common real-valued domain (both expressions are total under protected semantics and share the x3**(1/4) domain restriction). This is a value difference, not a domain-only difference, so it is a counterexample requiring fail.
review.counterexample: x3=1e-4, x0=1: original subterm log(sqrt(x3))=log(0.01)≈-4.6052, proposed subterm log(x3)/2=0 (protected fallback since |x3|=1e-4<=0.001); the inner sqrt argument in the denominator shifts by ≈4.605 (sqrt ≈2.146 vs ≈1e-4), changing the overall value far beyond tolerance.
